faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: What people usually ask before we start

items.question: What kind of projects do you build?
items.answer: Web platforms for operations management, B2B commerce, tools for lead capture, and map-based or field data systems. I handle the full product: interface, backend, integrations, and deployment.

items.question: How do you quote?
items.answer: In phases. We first agree on the scope, deliverables, and timeline for each stage — so you can move forward step by step without committing the full budget upfront.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: Roughly 3 to 6 weeks, depending on scope and how quickly we can iterate on feedback. Larger projects are split into phases, each with its own timeline.

items.question: What do I need to get started?
items.answer: Ideally a concrete idea: what problem you want to solve, what features you need, and the scope you have in mind. It doesn't have to be perfect — we'll refine it in an initial conversation.

items.question: Do I need a technical background?
items.answer: No. You know your business; I translate that into a technical solution and explain the important decisions without unnecessary jargon.

items.question: What is your main stack?
items.answer: React, NestJS, and TypeScript, with MongoDB or PostgreSQL depending on the case. I choose tools based on maintainability, performance, and what the project needs to integrate.

items.question: Do you work remotely?
items.answer: Yes. I'm based in La Serena and work with clients across Chile and internationally via video call, email, or WhatsApp.

items.question: Do you offer post-launch support?
items.answer: Yes. We can agree on maintenance, improvements, or new integrations once the system is in production.

items.question: Where can I see your work?
items.answer: The projects section has real case studies with context, solution, and technologies used. You can also check my GitHub profile.

la-alpina-park.title: Operations Platform — La Alpina Park
la-alpina-park.subtitle: Software engineer & developer · Individual project · Motocross track
la-alpina-park.excerpt: System to manage riders, attendance, payments, and daily track operations with real-time indicators.
la-alpina-park.description: I designed and built end-to-end a web application for the track's daily operations: rider management, track day scheduling, attendance records, payments with transaction history, and a control panel with KPIs and charts for debtors and attendance.
la-alpina-park.problem: The track managed riders, track days, and payments in spreadsheets. There was no clear view of debtors, attendance, or how operations were performing. Each process — registrations, race-day attendance, collections, and payment follow-up — relied on manual records and scattered files.
la-alpina-park.solution: I defined the system architecture (SPA frontend and REST backend) and built a web platform where the team manages everything in one place: riders, scheduling, attendance, and payment movements. I implemented user administration with email password recovery, a dashboard with the numbers that matter, and charts for debtors and attendance. The stack is React and NestJS with MongoDB; I deployed the frontend on Vercel and the backend on Railway.
la-alpina-park.result: Daily operations moved to a production system with less reliance on spreadsheets and immediate visibility into the track's status. The team can schedule dates, record attendance, manage payments, and review indicators without leaving the platform.

ventas-fama.title: Commercial Platform — Ventas Fama
ventas-fama.subtitle: Software engineer & developer · Professional internship · Distribution company
ventas-fama.excerpt: ERP-connected platform for client maps, PDF catalogs, expiry alerts, and forms and analytics modules.
ventas-fama.description: I designed and built a web platform that complements a distribution company's internal ERP: territorial client visualization, automated PDF catalog generation, expiry alerts via WhatsApp and email, surveys and evaluations, and analysis of their results.
metrics: Interactive client map from ERP data
Expiry alerts via WhatsApp and email
ventas-fama.problem: Catalogs were built by hand in Canva — a slow, hard-to-scale process. Commercial data lived in the ERP, but there was no way to see clients' geographic dispersion for route planning, no automatic batch expiry alerts, and no structured channel for client and supplier surveys or to analyze those responses.
ventas-fama.solution: I built an application connected to the ERP via API to fetch client and product data; product images are uploaded on the platform. I developed an interactive map using OpenStreetMap libraries to visualize client distribution and support route planning. I implemented asynchronous PDF catalog generation from ERP data, expiry alerts sent via WhatsApp and email, a forms module for client and supplier surveys and evaluations, and a data analysis module for the collected responses. The platform includes role-based authentication and was deployed on Vercel and Railway.
ventas-fama.result: The team no longer depends on Canva for catalogs, has territorial visibility of their portfolio from ERP data, and receives automatic expiry alerts. Forms and data analysis let them evaluate clients and suppliers with information centralized on the platform.

laguna-roja.title: Lead Capture & Management — Laguna Roja
laguna-roja.subtitle: Software engineer & developer · Freelance · Real estate, Elqui Valley
laguna-roja.excerpt: Lead capture ecosystem for land plots: landing pages, CRM, and sales automation evolved across three phases.
laguna-roja.description: Freelance project for Laguna Roja Inmobiliaria built in three phases: landing pages on Hostinger connected to Kommo via Make, a migration API deployed on Railway during the move to Odoo, and current automation with n8n, Evolution API, OpenAI, and Google Calendar.
laguna-roja.problem: The real estate company captured prospects from digital campaigns, but the sales flow relied on manual tasks and the team changed CRM mid-project. They needed landing pages feeding the sales system, periodic team reports, and — after moving to Odoo — automation for first client contact, meeting scheduling, and operational alerts.
laguna-roja.solution: In phase one I built the landing pages, deployed them on Hostinger, and connected them to Kommo through webhooks in Make; I also set up an email reporting flow in Make. In phase two, while migrating from Kommo to Odoo, I developed a NestJS API deployed on Railway that moved leads from the old CRM to the new one during the transition. In phase three I updated the landing pages, replaced the Make webhook with one in n8n to connect them to Odoo, and integrated Evolution API and OpenAI for automated first contact with prospects. I also connected Google Calendar to schedule online Meet calls or in-person meetings at the real estate projects, migrated the alert system to n8n, and extended it so alerts also arrive via WhatsApp through Evolution API.
laguna-roja.result: The ecosystem evolved with each stage of the business: today the landing pages feed Odoo, the team receives alerts by email and WhatsApp, and first contact plus meeting scheduling are automated. The project is still in progress, with ongoing improvements to the commercial operation.

acamu.title: Commercial & Document Management — ACAMU
acamu.subtitle: Software engineer & developer · Individual project · Fruit exporter, Peru
acamu.excerpt: Single portal for admins, suppliers, and clients with document traceability per shipment.
acamu.description: I designed and built end-to-end a web platform to centralize document, commercial, and operational management for a fruit export company, connecting administrators, suppliers, and clients in a single portal with traceability per shipment.
acamu.problem: The export operation relied on scattered documents and limited visibility into certifications, orders, and shipments. Suppliers, clients, and the internal team worked with loose files, without a single record of the export cycle or alerts for pending documentation.
acamu.solution: I defined the system architecture (decoupled SPA frontend and REST backend), modeled the export business domain — supplier and packing plant certifications, purchase orders, payments, shipping documentation, and transport companies — and implemented role-based access, secure PDF uploads, automatic reminders for pending documentation, and email notifications. I deployed the frontend on Vercel and the backend on Railway.
acamu.result: All stakeholders operate in one place with less document friction and better shipment tracking. Certifications, orders, and shipments are traced on the platform, with reminders that reduce delays from incomplete documentation.

gp-performance.title: Operations System — GP-Performance
gp-performance.subtitle: Software engineer & developer · Individual project · Auto repair shop
gp-performance.excerpt: End-to-end system for work orders, inventory, invoicing, and cash flow.
gp-performance.description: I designed and built end-to-end a web application for the operational and commercial management of an auto repair shop, covering the full business cycle: clients and vehicles, work orders, quotes, inventory, sales, invoicing, and cash flow.
metrics: Full shop cycle in one system
gp-performance.problem: Clients, orders, inventory, and invoicing lived in separate tools, causing duplication and poor traceability. The shop had no single view of each order's status, available stock, or cash flow tied to services and sales.
gp-performance.solution: I defined the system architecture (NestJS REST backend and React SPA frontend), modeled the relational database in PostgreSQL, and built modules for clients and vehicles, work orders with status tracking, quotes, inventory with stock control, product and service sales, invoicing, cash flow, and client communications. I managed production deployment on Vercel and Railway.
gp-performance.result: The shop runs on a single production system with better order, stock, and cash flow tracking. From vehicle intake to invoicing, every step is recorded on the same platform.

uoct.title: UOCT Connect — Operations platform
uoct.subtitle: Lead developer & technical lead · Multidisciplinary team · Coquimbo Region
uoct.excerpt: Application to report road incidents on OpenStreetMap, coordinate teams in real time, and cross-reference Waze and CGE data.
uoct.description: I led the design and implementation of UOCT Connect, the web application for the Coquimbo Region traffic control operations unit: georeferenced incident reporting, OpenStreetMap-based maps, real-time chat per incident, and integrations with Waze and CGE.
uoct.problem: The unit needed to centralize incident reports with precise location, coordinate field teams, and rely on historical data for operational decisions. There was no single platform with a map, real-time communication per incident, or integration with external sources such as Waze traffic jams or CGE power outages.
uoct.solution: I defined the system architecture (REST/WebSockets backend and SPA frontend), coordinated the development team, and built UOCT Connect with OpenStreetMap-based maps, real-time incident monitoring, and a real-time chat tied to each incident. I integrated Waze to visualize and store reliable traffic jams and road incidents on the platform, and connected CGE to visualize and record power outages. I managed production deployment on local UOCT infrastructure with Docker Compose and Jenkins.
uoct.result: The UOCT runs UOCT Connect in production to record, visualize, and analyze incidents across the region. The operations team coordinates responses with per-incident chat, monitors real-time maps, and cross-references Waze data and CGE power outages for a fuller picture of the territory.
